India's top diplomat in UAE for talks
Indian Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar has met United Arab Emirates' Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan while on a visit to Abu Dhabi.
Jaishankar called the meeting "warm and productive" in a post on X and said that the two sides discussed bilateral and global issues.
The Indian top diplomat's three-day visit to the UAE began on Wednesday.
A statement released by the Foreign Ministry in New Delhi earlier this week said the bilateral talks would review the progress of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between India and the UAE.
Jaishankar is also taking part in the Raisina Middle East forum in Abu Dhabi, co-hosted by New Delhi-based think tank Observer Research Foundation and the foreign ministries of India and the UAE.

He said a discussion with Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan at the event underpinned the importance of recognizing the increasing pace of change in the global order, highlighting that it reflects "long term trends and immediate shocks."

"Countries respond as per their specific situation. New partnerships and fresh options are inevitably explored in that pursuit," he said, adding that it involved going beyond "traditional comfort zones and developing sharper strategic awareness."
Jaishankar also called for an urgent "reform of multilateralism," which he said could be supported through a more robust "minilateralism."

On Wednesday, Jaishankar also met Georgian Foreign Minister Maka Botchorishvili in Abu Dhabi and discussed ways to further deepen bilateral cooperation in areas such as business, connectivity and culture.
